audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill, Singed, Singed, Skill, Skill, Singed, Singed and disagrees with its own prose in four places. early calls levels 1-2 'genuinely dangerous' and whys[0] and whys[1] both describe Vayne winning them, yet level 1 is Skill and level 2 is Singed. whys[3] and whys[4] describe the proxy window and 'your clearest kill window' at 6, yet both are scored Skill. whys[6] says a Guinsoo's Vayne 'outpaces your side-lane threat', yet the two-item stage is scored Singed.
audit.why: Emerald+ 55.14% over 1509 games. The packet chart is Vayne, Vayne, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed, Vayne, which is exactly what the seven why lines already say — Vayne owns the ranged early and the itemised late, Singed owns everything in between. The current chart has the shape inverted at both ends.
audit.corrected: Whole chart moved as one group to the packet read across both layers, with the five flipped stages' why lines rewritten.
sources: champ-data/content/singed.js (early, whys[0], whys[1], whys[3], whys[4], whys[6])

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] is built on Vayne 'burning Tumble repositioning' and whys[1] on her being unable to keep using it. Tumble's cooldown is 6/5/4/3/2, and Final Hour reduces it further.
audit.why: This is the load-bearing error in the entry. A six-second cooldown that becomes two seconds is not a resource you outlast — the advice 'wait until she burns Tumble' tells a Singed to wait for something that is never down. The cooldown that IS punishable is Condemn at 20/18/16/14/12, and the entry never puts a number on it despite naming it the matchup-defining ability in focus, loading, breakdown.cooldowns and report. Final Hour is 100/85/70 against Insanity Potion's flat 100, so from rank 2 her ultimate cycles faster than yours.
audit.corrected: Play off Condemn's 20s at rank 1, never off Tumble's 6s. Numbers written into spikes[1], whys[1], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and dosFull[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] tells the player Vayne can 'kite backward through Tumble invisibility' as an unconditional option. Riot's Final Hour text: 'Vayne gains increased Attack Damage, Invisibility during Tumble, reduced Tumble cooldown, and more bonus Move Speed from Night Hunter.'
audit.why: Tumble grants no invisibility of its own — it is granted by Final Hour and only while Final Hour is running. Stated unconditionally it makes the pre-6 lane sound unwinnable and, worse, it removes the tell: the invisibility appearing IS the cue that her ultimate is up, which is the single most useful read a Singed can take off her. It also means the vanish is on a 100/85/70 clock, not permanent.
audit.corrected: Tumble only vanishes her while Final Hour is active — the vanish is the tell that her ultimate is running.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0], whys[2] and spikes[1] all describe 'Mega Adhesive's root' as a property of the goo. Mega Adhesive slows and grounds; it does not root.
audit.why: Riot's Fling text: 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' The root is a two-step sequence with a required order — goo on the ground, then Fling into it. Against Vayne specifically the order is the entire play, because Fling's range is 125 and hers is 750: you get one contact, and spending it in the wrong order gets you nothing but a Condemn into the wall behind you.
audit.corrected: Goo first, then Fling into it. Landing in the Mega Adhesive is what roots her.

audit.whatIsWrong: Night Hunter is never mentioned. Riot's text: 'Vayne ruthlessly hunts evil-doers, gaining Move Speed when moving toward nearby enemy champions.' Fling and Condemn are also both displacement and the page never connects them.
audit.why: Night Hunter is directional — she gets the bonus speed closing on you and nothing at all running away, and Final Hour increases only that same closing bonus. That is the mechanical reason a Singed can chase her at all once Insanity Potion is up, and it is the justification for the level-6 all-in the page already recommends without explaining. Separately, the _missing rule for this pair flags that both sides carry displacement: Fling and Condemn cancel each other's setup, so whoever lands first owns the trade — and hers stuns on terrain contact while yours does not.
audit.corrected: Night Hunter only speeds her toward you, never away — that is why the level-6 chase works. Fling versus Condemn: whoever lands first owns the trade.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (Night Hunter, Final Hour, Condemn knockup/hardCC)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Condemn with no number and fills the rest with placeholders.
audit.why: Condemn at 20s rank 1 is the only cooldown in her kit worth tracking; Tumble at 6s down to 2s is effectively always available and Silver Bolts has no cooldown at all. A page that says 'track it' without the number gives the player nothing to count.

notes: The entry's central piece of advice was unworkable: spikes[1] and whys[1] both told the player to commit 'once Vayne burns Tumble', and Tumble is 6/5/4/3/2 seconds and drops further under Final Hour. It is never burnt. Repointed the whole plan at Condemn (20/18/16/14/12, 550 range), which is the only long cooldown in her kit and which the entry already named matchup-defining without ever printing the number. Second correction: wants.foe[2] presented Tumble invisibility as unconditional — Riot grants it through Final Hour only, so the vanish is itself the tell that her 100/85/70 ultimate is running. Third: 'Mega Adhesive's root' appeared in three fields; the goo slows and grounds, and Fling landing a target IN the goo is what roots. Added Night Hunter, which was absent — it only speeds her toward you, never away, which is the actual mechanism behind the level-6 chase the page already recommends. Chart moved to the packet read (Vayne, Vayne, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed, Vayne); the old one scored the two stages her own why lines give to Vayne as Singed's, and vice versa. Also fixed a misgendering in phases[4].why ('farming where he is not') and dontsFull[0].d ('half his win condition'). NOT ASSERTED: Mega Adhesive grounds and Tumble is a dash in play, but vayne.json carries no dash flag on Tumble and _missing has no enemy-dash-deniable rule for this pair, so I did not claim the goo denies it. Condemn's kit flags include 'terrain: creates terrain' — that is a tooltip-parsing misfire, Riot's text is about the target colliding with existing terrain, and I wrote nothing from it.
